how: Members supply several starts by setting an anchor, carving out a corner, and proposing profession-colored figures.
Members rally fellow dwarves and request help with particular additions to the shared display.
Willing newcomers require instruction in choosing colors and placing pixels before their offers of help become workable participation.
A request for help on the dead goblin receives a brief acceptance framed as a reassigned task.
Members judge available territory, coordination, and defensible scale insufficient for some proposed extensions.
A five-minute-wait notice informs participants about placement conditions without demonstrating an effect on recruitment or output.
Contributors revise figures, assign profession colors, change priorities, and drop a proposal in favor of work already underway.
Members report completed parts and individual progress, including a mug, one lettering pixel, and an unfinished subreddit sign.
Anchor coordinates, grids, and visible goals let participants locate and compare their contributions.
Changed targets must be accessible to relevant placers, including people unable to use the planning chat.

statement: Relaying decisions between chat and public threads
how: Plans and decisions move into chat and return as reports or targets, while public threads also carry proposals back into chat.
Maintaining an intended revision requires its goal to reach repairers who otherwise mistake planned changes for invasion.
Members recruit script users, propose defensive script adjustments, and debate whether automation preserves work or removes its fun.
Deliberate coordination can consist of reported chat decisions about repair and expansion without documented elections or formal leadership.
A single room with reported decisions cannot test the stated cross-room prevalence of decided order.
Members repeatedly clean, repair, and defend existing figures against changed colors and the Void.
Maintenance can proceed through independent visual repair without joining communication channels.
Participants identify friendly fire and mistaken repairs when apparently hostile pixels belong to an intended design.
Neighbors negotiate reciprocal limits, noninterference, truces, and proposed relocation or rebuilding.
Members welcome neighbors, remind builders to respect agreed limits, return disputed art, and stop repairing an agreed recoloring.
Respecting an agreed design also depends on repairers learning that a perceived invasion is intentional.
Neighbors offer joint defense, barter construction help for preserved pixels, and receive thanks for their support.
Named alliances and collaboration appear through an alliance inquiry, Minecraft cooperation, and an ally-colored design returned from chat.
A member reports carrying a conditional border agreement back from another group's thread.
Territorial requests and reciprocal borders do not establish continuing host authority over a guest work.
Movement and rebuilding proposals do not establish both prior erasure and a completed collective relocation.
Agreement reports and access objections contain no explicit denial that an envoy may commit the room.
Game language supplies forms for recruitment, task acceptance, canvas storytelling, and restraint toward other works.
Applying inherited lore to a newly named opponent does not establish a pre-canvas tie that selected that opponent.
Territorial conflict and fandom insults do not establish a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Temporary permission, megathread proposals, spam objections, defenses of local posting, and unsubscribing contest the host's boundary around canvas talk.
One participant turns irritation about canvas spam into a claim of helping the destructive Void.
A participant explicitly explains claimed help for destructive canvas action through irritation with host posting.
A canvas joke and a temporary posting rule do not establish a host takeover or deceptive April Fools license.
Contributors announce completion, thank participants, and name the finished work Placemurdered.
Participants share a timelapse and recount conflict, treaties, concessions, and the named final display.
A post-close report of pixels contributed to an ally records earlier labor rather than demonstrating fresh placement after the stop.

statement: Returning canvas attention to the ordinary community
how: A short redirect makes the game findable while the broader chat welcomes event-channel arrivals, without establishing lasting membership conversion.
Welcoming arrivals before closure does not establish a later decision or outcome about retaining the temporary effort.
Final naming and retrospective war accounts do not demonstrate contest over a cleaned canvas copy or correction of shared history.
Members call a coordinated strike against a neighbor's flag, while a separate contributor admits a joke alteration.
Participants carry conflict into lore-based insults, marching imagery, and a claimed memorial to an opponent's defeat.
A request for help writing a slogan receives a direct report of a pixel contributed to its lettering.
The initial anchor and collective call occur together, giving members a proposed work to answer.
An invitation to build and maintain a figure is followed by a stated need to concentrate on cleaning it.
Upkeep can overlap initial construction rather than wait until the whole mark is completed.
A perceived neighboring threat receives a direct accommodation and joint-defense offer.
A reported noninterference agreement receives a direct welcome and later reminders to leave the neighboring logo alone.
Automation is explicitly defended for overnight coverage, while the claimed manual-capacity threshold remains unmeasured.
The ally-pattern revision receives acceptance from a repairer and an explicit completion announcement within the same thread.
Treat recording as concurrent with construction when a timelapse is shared before later pieces are complete.
The timelapse and completion reports show recording and celebration but do not establish celebration as the cause of recording.
The pre-close welcome is not linked to a record of the work or a demonstrated later retention decision.
Capacity objections and relocation proposals lack a supported causal connection to a completed collective move.
Designs, coordinates, and a grid proposal do not establish a template settling a preceding design dispute.
A request for dead-goblin help receives a brief acceptance that asks for nothing back.
The observed acceptance pair supports a written response without testing normative obligation, refusal preferences, or unrecorded placement answers.
Joint-defense offers and requests for neighbor help do not establish a shortage of hands causing those exchanges.
Accommodation and offered help can occupy one turn rather than two separately observed stages.
Earlier recruitment and later strike calls do not identify recruits becoming attackers because of the initial call.
Returning disputed art and recounting rebuilding after war do not establish the proposed reasoned-refusal mechanism as an attack-call response pair.
A local truce proposal answers an appeal for coexistence, while separate attack posts cannot be assigned as its cause.
Attack calls and later rival-directed taunts coexist without proving that a particular call caused the taunt.
Joint defense is explicitly offered against shared threats, but the coalition's internal formation remains unseen.
Posting objections name a flood of event content without isolating recruitment calls as the sole source of that flood.
Visible agreements and unseen chat deliberations do not establish a subsequent dispute over who may bind the room.
